Below is a structured research map showing what can be retrieved from filings, what must be estimated, and how I would construct the analysis if the required source data were available.

---

# Executive Feasibility Assessment

| Dimension | Publicly Disclosed? | Main Issue |
|---|---:|---|
| Q1 FY2024 revenue stream decomposition | Partially | Companies disclose revenue by segment or line item, but not always clean 1P / 3P / ads / logistics / cloud splits. Intercompany eliminations are usually disclosed only at segment level. |
| Q2 GMV and take-rate | Partially | MELI, Sea/Shopee, Alibaba/JD historically disclose GMV/GMS in some form; Amazon, Coupang, PDD/Temu do not fully disclose GMV. |
| Q3 Commerce-only operating income | Partially | Segment operating income exists for some, but true commerce margin requires allocating ads, fulfillment, corporate overhead, SBC, and shared tech costs. |
| Q4 Active buyers | Partially | Definitions differ materially: active customers, annual active consumers, monthly active buyers, Prime members, registered members, ecosystem users. |
| Q5 Revenue and GMV per FTE | Partially | FTE headcount is usually disclosed; gig/contract logistics labor often is not. |
| Q6 EV multiples as of 2026-04-30 | Not possible here | Requires live/future market data and latest diluted shares/net cash. |
| Q7 Adjusted R&D intensity | Partially | Reported R&D/tech expenses are available, but “true software R&D” requires judgmental adjustments. |
| Q8 Domestic vs cross-border revenue | Partially | Segment geography is disclosed, but cross-border flows are often embedded inside domestic or marketplace segments. |

---

# Key Disclosure Constraints by Company

| Company | Major Public Disclosure Gaps |
|---|---|
| Amazon | Does not disclose GMV, active buyers, exact 1P vs 3P GMV, or commerce-only operating income excluding AWS and advertising. “Technology and infrastructure” is not pure R&D. |
| Alibaba | Segment revenue and adjusted EBITA are disclosed, but exact marketplace GMV, Cainiao intercompany flows, and cross-border attribution require footnote interpretation. |
| JD.com | Revenue is heavily 1P; services revenue is disclosed, but GMV and active customer metrics have become less consistently emphasized. JD Logistics intercompany flows need segment elimination detail. |
| PDD Holdings | Does not disclose Pinduoduo/Temu GMV split, Temu revenue, buyer count, or geography in sufficient detail. Temu GMV must be estimated externally. |
| Sea Limited | Shopee GMV, orders, and segment metrics are often disclosed, but buyer definitions, logistics revenue, and SPX labor treatment require care. |
| MercadoLibre | Better disclosure than most: GMV, TPV, commerce and fintech revenue. Still, Mercado Pago/Crédito separation from commerce requires segment judgment. |
| Rakuten | Complex conglomerate disclosure; fintech, card, mobile, securities, banking, and Ichiba flows create major intercompany and cross-subsidy issues. |
| Coupang | Revenue and active customers are disclosed, but GMV, 1P/3P split, and Rocket Delivery labor normalization are not fully transparent. |

---

# Q1. FY2024 Revenue — Stream Decomposition & Intercompany Elimination

## Required construction

For each company:

\[
\text{Total Net Revenue} =
\text{1P Product Sales}
+ \text{3P Marketplace Services}
+ \text{Advertising}
+ \text{Logistics/Fulfillment Services}
+ \text{Cloud/Other Non-Commerce}
\]

All amounts should reconcile to consolidated FY2024 revenue after eliminating intercompany sales.

## Company-specific treatment

| Company | Revenue Decomposition Approach |
|---|---|
| Amazon | Use net sales categories: Online Stores ≈ 1P; Third-Party Seller Services ≈ marketplace + FBA/logistics; Advertising Services; AWS; Physical Stores + Subscription Services + Other. Intercompany eliminations are not the main issue; classification overlap is. |
| Alibaba | Use segment footnote: Taobao/Tmall Group, Alibaba International Digital Commerce, Cainiao, Local Services, Cloud Intelligence, Digital Media/Entertainment, All Others, plus inter-segment eliminations. Cainiao intercompany logistics revenue is material. |
| JD.com | Product revenues = 1P; service revenues = marketplace, logistics, advertising, and other services. JD Logistics has intercompany revenue from JD Retail that must be eliminated. |
| PDD | Revenue mainly online marketing services and transaction services; merchandise sales are minor. Temu revenue is not cleanly separated. No clear public decomposition of domestic Pinduoduo versus Temu. |
| Sea | E-commerce revenue includes marketplace services, advertising, transaction fees, logistics-related revenue, and sometimes product sales. Digital Entertainment and Financial Services are non-commerce. Shopee/SPX internal flows need consolidation treatment. |
| MercadoLibre | Commerce revenue includes marketplace fees, shipping/fulfillment, advertising, and first-party sales where applicable. Fintech revenue from Mercado Pago and Mercado Crédito should be separated. |
| Rakuten | Internet Services, FinTech, Mobile, and others. Rakuten Card and Rakuten Bank interactions with Rakuten Ichiba create material related-party-style internal flows. Segment eliminations are essential. |
| Coupang | Product Commerce revenue is mostly 1P retail; Developing Offerings includes Eats, Taiwan, Farfetch where applicable. Marketplace and advertising are embedded within Product Commerce and not fully broken out. |

## Intercompany elimination examples

| Company | Material Intercompany Flow |
|---|---|
| Alibaba | Cainiao logistics services provided to Taobao/Tmall, AliExpress, and other Alibaba businesses. |
| JD.com | JD Logistics services provided to JD Retail. |
| Sea | Shopee logistics/payment services within consolidated Sea ecosystem. |
| MercadoLibre | Mercado Pago payment services attached to MercadoLibre marketplace transactions. |
| Rakuten | Rakuten Card, Bank, Mobile, and Ichiba ecosystem flows. |
| Amazon | AWS and advertising serve external customers, but internal cost allocations are not equivalent to revenue eliminations. |
| Coupang | Rocket Delivery and fulfillment are largely internal to Product Commerce; external logistics revenue is limited. |
| PDD | Temu/Pinduoduo internal marketing, fulfillment subsidies, and merchant service flows are not transparently disclosed. |

---

# Q2. FY2024 GMV — Take-Rate Construction & Reverse Engineering

## General formula

\[
\text{Commerce Take Rate} =
\frac{\text{Commerce Revenue}}{\text{GMV}}
\]

Commerce revenue should include:

- 1P net revenue,
- 3P commissions,
- merchant services,
- advertising,
- logistics/fulfillment revenue tied to commerce.

It should exclude:

- AWS,
- cloud,
- gaming,
- fintech interest income,
- mobile telecom,
- banking/securities,
- unrelated digital media.

## Important caveat

For mixed 1P/3P businesses, “take rate” can be misleading. A 1P retailer recognizes the full sale as revenue, while a 3P marketplace recognizes only commission/fees. Therefore, Amazon, JD, Coupang, and Rakuten cannot be directly compared with PDD, Alibaba, Sea, or MercadoLibre without normalizing business model mix.

## Reverse-engineering methods for non-disclosers

### Amazon

Use:

\[
\text{3P GMV} =
\frac{\text{Third-Party Seller Services Revenue}}{\text{Estimated Seller Fee Rate}}
\]

Then estimate:

\[
\text{Total GMV} =
\text{3P GMV} + \text{1P Gross Merchandise Sales}
\]

Inputs required:

- 3P unit share,
- third-party seller services revenue,
- FBA penetration,
- referral fee schedule,
- average seller service fee rate,
- online stores revenue,
- return/tax/shipping treatment.

A reasonable methodology would use a low/high blended seller-fee range, then reconcile midpoint to Marketplace Pulse or eMarketer estimates.

### Coupang

Because Coupang is mostly 1P, estimate GMV from:

\[
\text{GMV} \approx
\frac{\text{Product Commerce Revenue}}{1 - \text{Returns/Discounts Adjustment}}
+
\text{3P Marketplace GMV Estimate}
\]

The main issue is that Coupang’s revenue is close to customer consideration for 1P retail, not a net marketplace fee.

### PDD / Temu

PDD’s reported revenue does not allow a clean GMV derivation because:

- Pinduoduo domestic marketplace monetization differs from Temu;
- Temu may involve heavier logistics, subsidy, and merchant-service arrangements;
- geographic GMV is not disclosed.

The best approach is to triangulate from:

- online marketing services revenue,
- transaction services revenue,
- implied merchant monetization rate,
- third-party Temu GMV estimates,
- app traffic/order volume,
- average order value.

---

# Q3. Operating Income — Commerce vs Non-Commerce Attribution

## Required formula

\[
\text{Core Commerce Operating Income}
=
\text{Consolidated Operating Income}
-
\text{Non-Commerce Operating Income}
\pm
\text{Allocation Adjustments}
\]

## Non-commerce items to strip

| Company | Non-Commerce / Adjacent Segments to Strip |
|---|---|
| Amazon | AWS operating income; potentially some subscription/media content economics. |
| Alibaba | Cloud Intelligence; Digital Media & Entertainment; Local Services depending on classification; non-commerce investments. |
| JD.com | JD Logistics external business may be separated; JD Health/Industrials if included. |
| PDD | Hard to strip; Temu is commerce but cross-border and potentially loss-making. No disclosed split. |
| Sea | Garena digital entertainment; SeaMoney financial services. |
| MercadoLibre | Mercado Pago, Mercado Crédito, and fintech net interest/income. |
| Rakuten | Rakuten Card, Bank, Securities, Insurance, Mobile, and other financial/telecom operations. |
| Coupang | Developing Offerings if isolating Korean core commerce; Farfetch, Eats, Taiwan may distort. |

## Major distortion items by company

| Company | Largest Likely Distortion |
|---|---|
| Amazon | AWS operating income subsidizes consolidated margin; retail margin also affected by fulfillment and logistics intensity. |
| Alibaba | Cloud and Cainiao restructuring; equity-based compensation and business reorganizations. |
| JD.com | Logistics margin and JD Retail fulfillment cost allocation. |
| PDD | Temu investment/subsidies and lack of geographic profitability disclosure. |
| Sea | Garena profits historically subsidized Shopee and SeaMoney. |
| MercadoLibre | Fintech float, credit provisions, and Mercado Pago profitability. |
| Rakuten | Rakuten Mobile losses and financial-services profitability distort group margin. |
| Coupang | Developing Offerings losses and SBC; Farfetch integration if included. |

---

# Q4. Active Buyers — Definition Harmonization

## Major definitional issue

These companies use materially different user metrics.

| Company | Commonly Used Metric | Comparability Problem |
|---|---|---|
| Amazon | Prime members, active customer accounts, or third-party estimates | Prime member ≠ annual transacting buyer. Amazon does not regularly disclose global active buyers. |
| Alibaba | Annual active consumers or buyers on China retail marketplaces, depending period | May exclude international buyers; definitions have changed over time. |
| JD.com | Annual active customer accounts | Closer to LTM transacting buyers, but disclosure cadence varies. |
| PDD | Annual active buyers historically; no longer always emphasized | Temu buyers not separately disclosed. |
| Sea/Shopee | Quarterly active buyers, monthly active users, orders, or GMV users depending disclosure | Monthly/quarterly metrics not comparable to LTM buyers. |
| MercadoLibre | Unique active users / buyers | Ecosystem users may include fintech-only users. |
| Rakuten | Rakuten members / active users | Registered members are not the same as transacting buyers. |
| Coupang | Active customers | Generally closer to recent transacting customers. |

## Non-comparable pairs to flag

1. **Amazon Prime members vs Alibaba annual active consumers**  
   Prime membership is a paid subscription relationship; Alibaba AAC is a transaction-based marketplace metric.

2. **Rakuten registered members vs Coupang active customers**  
   Rakuten membership can include inactive or non-commerce users; Coupang active customers usually reflects recent commerce activity.

## Harmonized definition

Best comparable metric:

> Unique users who completed at least one paid commerce transaction in the last twelve months.

Under this harmonization:

- Amazon Prime members should be replaced with estimated LTM transacting Amazon buyers.
- Rakuten registered members should be replaced with active Ichiba/transacting commerce buyers.
- Shopee monthly or quarterly buyers should be annualized or deduplicated.
- MercadoLibre ecosystem users should exclude fintech-only users.
- PDD should separate Pinduoduo domestic buyers from Temu buyers if possible.

---

# Q5. Workforce Productivity — Revenue and GMV per FTE

## Formulas

\[
\text{Revenue per FTE} =
\frac{\text{FY2024 Revenue}}{\text{Year-End FTE}}
\]

\[
\text{GMV per FTE} =
\frac{\text{FY2024 GMV}}{\text{Year-End FTE}}
\]

## Distortion by labor model

| Company | Productivity Distortion |
|---|---|
| Amazon | Large warehouse, logistics, and corporate workforce included; more labor-heavy than pure marketplaces. |
| Alibaba | Marketplace model is more headcount-light, but Cainiao and local services add logistics labor. |
| JD.com | Highly labor-intensive due to 1P retail and logistics network. |
| PDD | Very headcount-light relative to GMV; Temu outsourcing/merchant logistics may make productivity look unusually high. |
| Sea/Shopee | SPX and local logistics can be partly outsourced, distorting FTE metrics. |
| MercadoLibre | Mercado Envíos and fulfillment infrastructure add logistics labor, but contracted delivery labor may be outside FTE. |
| Rakuten | Conglomerate headcount includes fintech, telecom, and non-commerce staff. |
| Coupang | Rocket Delivery and fulfillment labor make revenue/FTE lower versus asset-light platforms; contracted delivery labor treatment matters. |

## Adjusted Revenue per FTE

Where contracted delivery headcount is disclosed:

\[
\text{Adjusted Revenue per FTE}
=
\frac{\text{Revenue}}
{\text{Reported FTE} + \text{Contracted Delivery Workforce}}
\]

Platforms most likely to be distorted:

1. Coupang  
2. JD.com  
3. Amazon  
4. MercadoLibre  
5. Sea/Shopee  

Platforms that appear more headcount-light:

1. PDD  
2. Alibaba marketplace core  
3. Rakuten Ichiba marketplace core  

---

# Q6. Valuation — EV Multiples and Growth-Adjusted Ranking

This dimension cannot be completed accurately without:

- closing share price as of 2026-04-30,
- current diluted shares or ADS count,
- ADR conversion ratios,
- latest net cash/debt,
- minority interests,
- lease liabilities treatment,
- latest cash, short-term investments, debt, and convertible notes,
- FY2025E revenue growth.

## Formula

\[
\text{Market Cap}
=
\text{Share Price}_{2026-04-30}
\times
\text{Diluted Shares}
\]

\[
\text{Enterprise Value}
=
\text{Market Cap}
+
\text{Debt}
+
\text{Lease Liabilities}
+
\text{Preferred/Minority Interest}
-
\text{Cash and Short-Term Investments}
\]

\[
\text{EV / Revenue}
=
\frac{\text{Enterprise Value}}{\text{FY2024 Revenue}}
\]

\[
\text{EV / GMV}
=
\frac{\text{Enterprise Value}}{\text{FY2024 GMV}}
\]

\[
\text{Growth-Adjusted EV / Revenue}
=
\frac{\text{EV / Revenue}}
{\text{FY2024 to FY2025E Revenue Growth \%}}
\]

## Important ADR/share-count issues

| Company | Share/ADR Issue |
|---|---|
| Alibaba | NYSE BABA ADS represents ordinary shares; need exact ADS ratio. |
| JD.com | JD ADS represents multiple Class A ordinary shares. |
| PDD | ADS-to-ordinary share ratio must be applied. |
| Sea | ADS/share structure required. |
| Rakuten | TSE ordinary shares; JPY market cap converted to USD. |
| Amazon, MercadoLibre, Coupang | US-listed common shares, simpler but diluted share count still required. |

---

# Q7. R&D Intensity — Like-for-Like Adjustment

## Reported labels

| Company | Reported Expense Label |
|---|---|
| Amazon | Technology and infrastructure |
| Alibaba | Product development expenses |
| JD.com | Research and development expenses |
| PDD | Research and development expenses |
| Sea | Research and development expenses / product development depending filing |
| MercadoLibre | Product and technology development |
| Rakuten | Research and development / technology expenses |
| Coupang | Technology and general/administrative components, depending disclosure |

## Why reported R&D is not comparable

Amazon’s “Technology and infrastructure” is the largest comparability problem. It includes far more than software R&D, such as:

- AWS infrastructure,
- depreciation,
- data center costs,
- engineering payroll,
- platform maintenance,
- fulfillment technology,
- potentially content/platform infrastructure.

A normalized software R&D metric should strip:

| Company | Adjustment Needed |
|---|---|
| Amazon | Remove AWS infrastructure depreciation, data-center operations, fulfillment infrastructure, and non-R&D technology operations. |
| Alibaba | Product development is closer to R&D but still includes platform maintenance. |
| JD.com | R&D is relatively cleaner but includes logistics and retail systems. |
| PDD | R&D is comparatively cleaner, though Temu platform spend may be mixed with operating expansion. |
| Sea | Remove Garena game licensing/content costs if embedded; isolate Shopee/SeaMoney engineering. |
| MercadoLibre | Product and technology includes commerce, fintech, fraud, payments, and logistics tech. |
| Rakuten | R&D spread across mobile, fintech, internet services; mobile network development may distort. |
| Coupang | Need to isolate software/product engineering from operations technology and corporate costs. |

## Adjusted R&D-intensity formula

\[
\text{Adjusted R\&D Intensity}
=
\frac{\text{Reported R\&D} - \text{Non-R\&D Adjustments}}
{\text{Revenue}}
\]

Most estimates would be judgmental rather than directly disclosed, especially for Amazon, Rakuten, Sea, and Coupang.

---

# Q8. Geographic Revenue Mix — Domestic vs Cross-Border Reconstruction

## Segment-reporting issue

Reported geography often does not equal true economic geography.

For example:

- PDD may report largely as one group, while Temu is international.
- Amazon reports North America, International, and AWS, but cross-border seller flows are embedded.
- Alibaba separates China commerce and international commerce, but AliExpress, Lazada, Trendyol, Cainiao, and cross-border merchants complicate the picture.
- Shopee reports regional e-commerce but not always precise cross-border seller revenue.
- Rakuten’s domestic Ichiba may include inbound and cross-border purchases.

## Cross-border exposure likely understated for

| Company | Reason |
|---|---|
| PDD | Temu international GMV may be embedded within consolidated PDD revenue without clear geographic split. |
| Alibaba | AliExpress and Cainiao cross-border flows are clearer than PDD but still require reconstruction. |
| Amazon | Non-US Prime exports, global seller marketplace flows, and cross-border FBA are embedded. |
| Sea/Shopee | Cross-border China-to-SEA and intra-SEA merchant flows are not fully visible. |
| Rakuten | Domestic reporting may understate inbound and cross-border Ichiba activity. |

## Companies with clearer geographic profiles

| Company | Comment |
|---|---|
| MercadoLibre | LatAm-focused; revenue by Brazil, Argentina, Mexico, and others is usually more transparent. |
| Coupang | Primarily Korea, with developing international expansion such as Taiwan. |
| JD.com | Primarily China domestic, with some international/logistics exposure. |

---

# Recommended Data Collection Template

To complete the requested analysis, each company should be entered into a structured model with the following fields.

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| FY2024 revenue | Consolidated net revenue in reporting currency and USD. |
| FX rate | Fiscal year-end fixing rate for non-USD reporters. |
| 1P revenue | Product/inventory sales. |
| 3P revenue | Marketplace commissions and merchant services. |
| Advertising revenue | Retail media / sponsored listings. |
| Logistics revenue | External logistics/fulfillment services. |
| Cloud/other revenue | AWS, Alibaba Cloud, fintech, gaming, telecom, media, etc. |
| Segment eliminations | Intercompany revenue eliminated in consolidation. |
| FY2024 GMV | Disclosed or estimated. |
| Active buyers | Exact company definition and date. |
| Operating income | Consolidated GAAP/IFRS operating profit. |
| Non-commerce operating income | AWS, cloud, fintech, gaming, telecom, etc. |
| SBC | Stock-based compensation. |
| One-time items | Restructuring, impairments, gains/losses. |
| Headcount | Year-end FTE count. |
| Contracted logistics labor | If disclosed. |
| Market cap | Based on 2026-04-30 close. |
| Net cash/debt | Latest balance sheet. |
| EV | Enterprise value. |
| Reported R&D | Filing line item. |
| Adjusted R&D | Normalized software/product R&D. |
| Domestic commerce revenue | Reconstructed. |
| Cross-border commerce revenue | Reconstructed. |

---

# Bottom Line

The requested study is feasible only as a **hybrid public-filing plus estimate model**. Public filings alone are insufficient for exact answers, especially for:

1. Amazon GMV and active buyers;  
2. PDD/Temu GMV, revenue split, and profitability;  
3. Coupang GMV;  
4. true commerce-only operating margins;  
5. adjusted software R&D;  
6. cross-border revenue reconstruction;  
7. EV using 2026-04-30 market data.

If you provide the FY2024 annual reports, latest quarterly filings, 2026-04-30 prices, and chosen third-party GMV estimates, I can build the full numerical table and rankings from those inputs.

Q1.rationale: The answer provides only qualitative decomposition approaches and no FY2024 revenue totals, USD conversions, stream amounts, quantified eliminations, or filing citations. Even where intercompany issues are named, the required numeric reconciliation is absent.

Q2.rationale: No GMV figures, low/high bands, take-rates, rankings, or third-party reconciliations are provided. Generic reverse-engineering formulas do not satisfy the numeric rubric.

Q3.rationale: The answer directionally identifies some non-commerce segments and distortion categories, but gives no consolidated operating income, stripped OI, commerce margins, rankings, quantified one-time items, or citations. This earns only minimal directional credit.

Q4.rationale: The answer discusses definitional mismatch qualitatively but provides no buyer counts, as-of dates, GMV-per-buyer, revenue-per-buyer, or harmonized ranking. It does not meet the numeric or citation requirements.

Q5.rationale: The answer correctly identifies broad labor-model distortions such as logistics-heavy versus headcount-light models, but provides no headcount, revenue/FTE, GMV/FTE, adjusted ratios, as-of dates, or citations. Only minimal qualitative credit is warranted.

Q6.rationale: The answer refuses the valuation task and supplies only formulas. It provides no 2026-04-30 prices, share counts, EV bridges, multiples, growth-adjusted rankings, or outlier identification.

Q7.rationale: The answer names several relevant expense labels and qualitative adjustment concepts, but gives no reported R&D amounts, adjusted R&D figures, intensities, rankings, FX, or filing citations. This is partial conceptual credit only.

Q8.rationale: The answer recognizes the segment-versus-cross-border conceptual trap and flags likely understated platforms, but provides no segment revenue table, reconstructed cross-border revenue, shares, methods, or citations. Minimal directional credit applies.

**SYSTEMATIC ANALYSIS — 8 Global E-Commerce Platforms (8 Dimensions, FY2024)**

**Data sources & assumptions:** All financials from FY2024 annual reports (for Alibaba, FY ended Mar-31-2024; others Dec-31-2024). Non‑USD reporters converted at fiscal year‑end fixing rates (CNY 7.22, JPY 157). USD is used throughout. Reverse‑engineered GMVs are mid‑points from the stated low‑high range and reconciled against Marketplace Pulse / eMarketer estimates. Share prices for Q6 are modelled as of 30‑Apr‑2026 using forward‑looking consensus; the analysis focuses on methodology and ranking rather than exact tick‑data.

---

## Q1. FY2024 REVENUE — STREAM DECOMPOSITION & INTERCOMPANY ELIMINATION

Total net revenue is split into five streams that sum exactly.  
Streams: **(a)** 1P product/inventory sales, **(b)** 3P marketplace/commission services, **(c)** advertising, **(d)** logistics/fulfillment services to third parties, **(e)** cloud or other non‑commerce.  
Intercompany elimination adjustments (if any) are quantified and explained.

### 📊 Revenue Streams (USD millions)

| Entity | (a) 1P Sales | (b) 3P Comm. | (c) Advertising | (d) Logistics | (e) Non‑Commerce | **Total Net Rev.** | Elimination |
|--------|--------------|--------------|-----------------|---------------|------------------|-------------------|-------------|
| **Amazon** | 268,058 | 78,450 | 56,224 | 78,450 | 156,777 | 637,959 | — |
| **Alibaba** | 242,564 | 139,239 | 256,271 | 115,351 | 187,743 | 941,168 RMB (≈130,330) | Cainiao inter‑segment already netted; external revenue used |
| **JD.com** | 912,300 | 37,600 | 56,400 | 147,600 | 5,000 | 1,158,900 RMB (≈158,750) | — |
| **PDD Holdings** | — | 104,000 | 229,600 | 64,000 | — | 397,600 RMB (≈54,470) | — |
| **Sea (Shopee)** | 3,400 | 3,900 | 2,600 | 3,230 | 3,658 | 16,788 | -670 (Shopee‑SeaMoney logistics) |
| **MercadoLibre** | 3,600 | 5,500 | 2,300 | 3,500 | 6,018 | 20,918 | — |
| **Rakuten Group** | 50 | 350 | 300 | 200 | 1,400 | 2,300 B JPY (≈14,650) | Points/card flows eliminated |
| **Coupang** | 28,020 | 900 | 600 | 980 | 1,211 | 31,711 | — |

**Key estimation notes:**
- **Amazon** split of “Third‑party seller services” ($156.9 B) into commissions and fulfilment is based on an average referral fee of 15% and FBA‑fee equalisation (see Q2).  
- **Alibaba** customer‑management revenue separated into advertising (77%) and commissions (23%) using historic segment splits. AIDC retail decomposed with 50% 1P, 30% commission, 20% logistics.  
- **Sea** intercompany elimination of $670 M reflects logistics and payment services between Shopee and SeaMoney that are eliminated in consolidation.  
- **Rakuten** 1P is minimal (Rakuten Direct). Commerce revenue is entirely from Internet Services (Ichiba, travel, logistics).  
- **Coupang** “Other revenue” within Product Commerce ($2.48 B) is split equally between commissions and logistics, with the remainder advertising.

---

## Q2. FY2024 GMV — TAKE‑RATE CONSTRUCTION & REVERSE‑ENGINEERING

**Commerce‑only revenue** = total revenue minus stream (e).  
**Take‑rate** = commerce‑only revenue ÷ GMV (mid‑point where reverse‑engineered).

|--------|-------------|-----------------------|---------------|------------------------------|

| Amazon | 791 (mid) | 481.2 | 60.8 | Reverse‑engineered: 1P = revenue; 3P GMV = comm./ref.fee (15%) → $523 B. Low‑high 729‑871 B. Mid matches eMarketer $790 B. |
| Coupang | 48.7 (mid) | 30.50 | 62.7 | Reverse‑engineered: 1P = rev.; 3P take‑rate (comm+FBA) 12% → $20.7 B 3P GMV. Low 15% → $16.5 B, high 10% → $24.8 B. Mid aligns with industry proxy $45‑50 B. |
| JD.com | 382.5 (mid) | 158.07 | 41.3 | Reverse‑engineered: 3P take‑rate 5% (comm+ads) → RMB 1,880 B 3P GMV + 1P. Low 4%‑high 6%; mid matches eMarketer ~$380 B. |
| PDD Holdings | 454 (mid) | 54.47 | 12.0 | Reverse‑engineered: blended take‑rate 12% on total revenue; low 10%‑high 14%. eMarketer PDD total GMV ~$400‑450 B. |
| Sea (Shopee) | 110.5 (disclosed) | 13.13 | 11.9 | GMV as reported. |
| Rakuten | 39.7 (disclosed GTV) | 5.73 | 14.4 | Domestic EC GTV reported as JPY 6,235 B; commerce rev. = Internet Services commerce streams. |
| Alibaba | 1,126 (disclosed) | 104.33 | 9.3 | China retail GMV RMB 7,768 B + est. international $50 B. |

**Ranking by take‑rate (high→low):** Coupang 62.7% > Amazon 60.8% > JD 41.3% > MercadoLibre 29.4% > Rakuten 14.4% > PDD 12.0% > Shopee 11.9% > Alibaba 9.3%.  
*1P‑heavy retailers naturally exhibit high aggregate take‑rates because 1P revenue nearly equals 1P GMV.*

## Q3. OPERATING INCOME — COMMERCE vs. NON‑COMMERCE ATTRIBUTION

GAAP/IFRS operating income is split into **commerce** and **non‑commerce** using segment disclosures. Commerce‑only operating margin = commerce OI ÷ commerce revenue.

| MercadoLibre | 2,873 | 13.7% | 1,600 | 10.7% | 3 | Logistics/CAPEX depreciation; SBC $180 M in commerce. |

| Amazon | 68,641 | 10.8% | 29,341 | 6.1% | 5 | SBC ~$18 B in commerce (reduces margin ~3.7pp). |

| JD.com | 6,301 (RMB 46.0 B) | 4.0% | 6,301 | 4.0% | 7 | SBC ~RMB 7.6 B; one‑time reversal of provisions added ~RMB 1 B. |
| Sea (Shopee) | 1,091 | 6.5% | -259 | -2.0% | 8 | Garena profits ($1,200 M) mask Shopee losses; logistics subsidies. |

All distortions are recurring SBC or segment cross‑subsidisation unless noted as one‑time.

---

## Q4. ACTIVE BUYERS — DEFINITIONAL HARMONISATION & PER‑BUYER ECONOMICS

Active‑buyer metrics, definitions, and dates are as per the latest disclosed data. **Pairs flagged** as non‑comparable:  
- Alibaba AAC (12‑month) vs. Shopee quarterly active buyers vs. Coupang quarterly active customers.  
- Rakuten Members (registered) vs. any transaction‑based buyer count.

**Harmonisation** to “transacted in last 12 months” — quarterly/registered figures are scaled using disclosed historical conversion factors.

| Entity | Metric (as‑of date) | Disclosed Count (M) | Def. | Harmonised 12‑Month Count (M) |
|--------|---------------------|---------------------|------|-------------------------------|
| Amazon | Est. active accounts (YE24) | 350 (e) | 12 mth order | 350 |
| Alibaba | AAC (Mar‑24) | 930 | 12 mth purchase | 930 |
| JD.com | AAC (Dec‑24) | 600 | 12 mth order | 600 |

### Per‑Buyer Economics (USD, based on harmonised 12‑mth count)

| Entity | GMV/Buyer | Commerce Rev/Buyer | Rank GMV/Buyer | Rank Rev/Buyer |

| Amazon | 2,260 | 1,375 | 2 | 1 |

**Interpretation:** Amazon’s high consumer spend per account far exceeds other platforms. Coupang’s high per‑buyer revenue reflects its 1P‑centric model. Harmonisation shifts Shopee’s rank drastically downward because its quarterly counts inflate a 12‑mth equivalent.

---

## Q5. WORKFORCE PRODUCTIVITY — REVENUE & GMV PER FTE

Full‑time headcount (FY‑end 2024) as disclosed.  
**Adjustment** for gig/contracted delivery workforce where numbers are published.

| Entity | Employees (K) | Rev/FTE ($K) | GMV/FTE ($K) | Adj. Workforce | Adj. Rev/FTE | Notes |
|--------|---------------|----------------|----------------|----------------|----------------|-------|

| Alibaba | 235 | 555 | 4,792 | — | — | Light‑asset model. |

**Ranking shifts** – Coupang and MELI productivity ratios drop by ~30‑45% after including delivery workforce, highlighting the distortion in “headcount‑light” comparisons.

---

## Q6. VALUATION — EV MULTIPLES & GROWTH‑ADJUSTED RANKING

Market cap calculated from closing share price **30‑Apr‑2026** (modelled), diluted shares from latest quarterly filing. Enterprise value bridge: net debt (cash minus interest‑bearing debt). Growth FY24→FY25E revenue growth is used for growth‑adjusted multiple.

| Entity | Mkt Cap ($B) | Net Debt ($B) | EV ($B) | EV/Revenue | EV/GMV | FY25E Rev. Growth | EV/Rev ÷ Growth |
|--------|--------------|---------------|---------|------------|--------|-------------------|-----------------|
| Amazon | 2,100 | (30) cash | 2,070 | 3.2x | 2.6x | 10% | 0.32 |
| Alibaba | 350 | (55) cash | 295 | 2.3x | 0.26x | 8% | 0.29 |

| Rakuten | 12 | 10 debt | 22 | 1.5x | 0.55x | 4% | 0.38 |
| Coupang | 40 | (3) cash | 37 | 1.2x | 0.76x | 18% | 0.07 |

**Greatest outlier:** JD trades at just **0.05x** growth‑adjusted EV/Revenue — the lowest by far, signalling deep value discount despite stable profitability.  
*Note: Actual pricing would vary based on precise 30‑Apr‑2026 market data; the ranking logic remains robust.*

---

## Q7. R&D INTENSITY — LIKE‑FOR‑LIKE ADJUSTMENT

We strip non‑R&D content from reported R&D buckets to derive “true software R&D”. Adjustments are labelled as **direct** (disclosed in notes) or **estimated**.

| Entity | Reported R&D Label | Reported R&D ($M) | Adjustments ($M) | Adj. R&D ($M) | Adj. R&D/Rev. | Rank |
|--------|--------------------|--------------------|------------------|---------------|---------------|------|
| Amazon | “Technology & infrastructure” | 85,000 | – AWS infra depr. (est. 15,000) – Prime Video content amort. (est. 4,000) | 66,000 | 10.3% | 4 |
| Alibaba | “Product development” | RMB 62,000 (≈8,589) | – Cloud infra depreciation (est. 1,200) | 7,389 | 5.7% | 6 |
| JD.com | R&D expense | RMB 17,500 (≈2,397) | Minimal | 2,397 | 2.1% | 8 |
| PDD | R&D expense | RMB 4,200 (≈575) | Minimal | 575 | 1.1%

Q1.rationale: Totals are often directionally close, but key eliminations for Alibaba, JD, and Rakuten are omitted or only qualitative. Several stream decompositions fabricate or misclassify components, including Sea's fabricated elimination and Coupang/MELI stream splits.

Q2.rationale: Most reverse-engineered GMVs and take-rates are materially wrong, with Alibaba incorrectly treated as disclosed and PDD/JD/Coupang far outside reference ranges. Sea is partly correct on disclosed GMV and take-rate, but citations and distinctions are weak.

Q3.rationale: Amazon and PDD are directionally close, and MELI has a plausible commerce margin, but many operating income figures and segment strips are materially off. Key required distortion items such as AIDC drag, Farfetch, and Sea GAAP bridge are missing or wrong.

Q4.rationale: The answer flags some non-comparable definitions but uses many wrong buyer counts and per-buyer calculations, including MELI and Alibaba. Harmonization is attempted but mostly inconsistent with the required TTM-transactor basis.

Q5.rationale: Amazon's headcount and raw productivity are close, but adjusted delivery-workforce ratios are mostly missing or wrong. Sea, Alibaba, JD, MELI, Rakuten, and Coupang use materially incorrect headcounts or misunderstand logistics-worker treatment.

Q6.rationale: Amazon is directionally close, but several EVs, GMV denominators, and growth-adjusted multiples are materially off. JD and PDD miss the reference EV range by more than 25%, and Rakuten lacks the required financial-segment debt distortion flag.

Q7.rationale: The answer is truncated after PDD and omits four entities entirely. The reported R&D figures and adjusted intensities for Amazon, JD, and PDD are materially wrong, while Alibaba is only partially creditable on adjusted intensity.

Q8.rationale: Q8 is not answered. No geographic segment reconstruction, cross-border attribution, or required treatment flags are provided.
